summary: This Wikipedia article covers the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES), a 16-bit home video game console developed by Nintendo. It describes the competitive backdrop of the late 1980s and early 1990s, including NEC's PC Engine, Sega's Mega Drive/Genesis, and the console war that followed. It also summarizes Nintendo's earlier licensing controls under the NES, the SNES's regional release dates and names, and its eventual market success.
one_line: Overview of the Super Nintendo Entertainment System, Nintendo's 16-bit console and its rivalry with Sega's Genesis.
key_facts: NEC Home Electronics launched the PC Engine in Japan in 1987 to compete with the Family Computer.
Sega Enterprises launched the Mega Drive in Japan in 1988.
The PC Engine and Mega Drive were launched in North America in 1989 as the TurboGrafx-16 and the Genesis respectively.
During the NES era, each third-party developer could release only up to five games per year.
In 1991, Acclaim began releasing games for both the NES and Sega's console, with most of Nintendo's other licensees following over the next several years.
Capcom and Square were the most notable holdouts against multi-platform releases.
Nintendo secured the first console conversion of Capcom's arcade classic Street Fighter II for SNES, which took over a year to make the transition to Genesis.
The Genesis represented an estimated 60% of the American 16-bit console market in June 1992.
Nintendo stated that it had sold more than 20 million SNES units in the U.S.
A 2014 Wedbush Securities report based on NPD sales data found the SNES ultimately outsold the Genesis in the U.S. market.
The Super Nintendo Entertainment System was released in Japan and South Korea in 1990, in North America in 1991, in Europe and Australasia in 1992, and in South America in 1993.
In Japan the system is called the Super Famicom, or SFC for short.
In South Korea the system is known as the Super Comboy and was distributed by Hyundai Electronics.
Several forms of regional lockout prevent the different SNES versions from being compatible with one another.
The SNES was released in Brazil on September 2, 1992, by Playtronic.
